title: The tame Galois sequence of a henselian discrete valuation field
statement:
Let $R$ be an excellent discrete valuation ring [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] which is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], with algebraically closed residue field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Put $F=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, choose a separable closure $F^{\mathrm{sep}}$, and equip $G=\operatorname{Gal}(F^{\mathrm{sep}}/F)$ with its profinite Krull topology. There is a closed normal subgroup $P$ and a continuous surjective homomorphism
$$
\theta:G\longrightarrow\prod_{r\text{ prime},\ r\neq p}(\mathbf Z_r,+)
$$
with kernel $P$, inducing an isomorphism of topological groups $G/P\cong\prod_{r\neq p}(\mathbf Z_r,+)$. Every finite continuous quotient of $P$ has order a power of $p$. Here $\mathbf Z_r$ denotes the $r$-adic integers [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], with inverse-limit topology $\mathbf Z_r=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\mathbf Z/r^n\mathbf Z$, and the displayed product has its product topology. The map $\theta$ may depend on choices of compatible roots of unity; no canonical trivialization of a Tate twist is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0BUB, lemma-structure-decomposition-separable-closure; specialization to a henselian DVR with algebraically closed residue field, with compatible roots of unity and the Chinese remainder decomposition of the tame inverse limit

proof.text: For every finite Galois subextension $L/F$ in $F^{\mathrm{sep}}$, let $B_L$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $L$. By [lem-exc-finite-dvr-tame-inertia], $B_L$ is finite over $R$, and its localizations at maximal ideals are DVRs with residue fields finite over $k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product] to $R\to B_L$. Discard any zero factors in the product decomposition. Since $B_L$ is a nonzero domain, at least one factor remains, and two remaining factors would give a nontrivial idempotent. Thus exactly one factor remains. Thus $B_L$ is local, hence itself a DVR; its residue field equals $k$ because $k$ is algebraically closed. Every $F$-automorphism stabilizes its unique maximal ideal and acts identically on that residue field, so $D_L=I_L=G_L=\operatorname{Gal}(L/F)$. The finite inertia lemma gives $P_L\triangleleft G_L$, a finite $p$-group, and a surjective uniformizer character $\chi_L:G_L\to\mu_{n_L}(k)$ with kernel $P_L$, where $e_L=q_Ln_L$, $q_L$ is a power of $p$ and $n_L$ is prime to $p$.

source.place: Tags 0BUA (lemma-structure-decomposition), finite-level setup, and 0BUB (lemma-structure-decomposition-separable-closure); more-algebra.tex Tags 09E8, 09EE and algebra.tex Tag 04GH

proof.text:
For $M\supseteq L$ finite Galois over $F$, let $\mathfrak n_M$ be the unique maximal ideal of $B_M$. By Step 1, $\mathfrak n_M$ contracts to the maximal ideal of $R$. Hence the quotient $B_L/(\mathfrak n_M\cap B_L)$ is a finite-dimensional domain over $k$, so it is a field: multiplication by any nonzero element is injective and hence surjective. Thus $\mathfrak n_M\cap B_L$ is maximal and equals the unique maximal ideal of $B_L$. Apply [lem-exc-finite-tame-character-tower]. Restriction is surjective on $G_M\to G_L$ and $P_M\to P_L$, and $n_L\mid n_M$. Replace the raw character by $\chi_{L,\mathrm{can}}=\chi_L^{q_L}$; the tower lemma gives
$$\chi_{L,\mathrm{can}}(\sigma|_L)=\chi_{M,\mathrm{can}}(\sigma)^{n_M/n_L}.$$
Thus the exact sequences $1\to P_L\to G_L\to\mu_{n_L}(k)\to1$ form an inverse system with surjective transitions on kernels, middle groups and quotients. The identity and composition laws on $G_L$ and $P_L$ are those of restriction. On the root groups, an identity inclusion has exponent $n_L/n_L=1$, and for $N\supseteq M\supseteq L$ the composite power exponent is $(n_N/n_M)(n_M/n_L)=n_N/n_L$, proving the same laws there. The indexing set is the set of finite Galois subfields in the fixed set $F^{\mathrm{sep}}$, ordered by inclusion; its nonemptiness and directedness are supplied by [lem-exc-galois-krull-finite-limit] (the bottom field and finite Galois composita).

source.place: Tag 0BUA (lemma-structure-decomposition), finite-system and canonical-character diagrams; more-algebra.tex Tags 0BU7 and 0BU8

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$. For each positive integer $m$ prime to $p$, [lem-exc-tame-root-extension] supplies a cyclic Galois field $L_m=F(\pi^{1/m})$ of degree and ramification index $m$, embedded in $F^{\mathrm{sep}}$. Consequently $n_{L_m}=m$. In particular every positive integer prime to $p$ occurs among the tame indices, not merely as an order bounded by a tame index. The same lemma also supplies the henselian lifting of the roots of unity required by the blueprint.

source.place: Tag 0BUB (lemma-structure-decomposition-separable-closure), uniformizer splitting-field paragraph; blueprint lem-exc-dvr-galois.proof.md, tame-level realization

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-infinite-tame-inverse-limit] to the exact inverse system in Step 2, with $I_L=G_L$ and $C_L=\mu_{n_L}(k)$. All its groups are finite, each $P_L$ is a $p$-group, and every transition is surjective by Step 2. Identify $G$ topologically with $\varprojlim_LG_L$ using [lem-exc-galois-krull-finite-limit] for the Galois extension $F^{\mathrm{sep}}/F$. We obtain a continuous surjection $G\to C=\varprojlim_L\mu_{n_L}(k)$ with kernel $P=\varprojlim_LP_L$, closed and normal in $G$, a topological isomorphism $G/P\cong C$, and the assertion that every finite continuous quotient of $P$ has $p$-power order.

source.place: Tag 0BUA (lemma-structure-decomposition), inverse-limit exactness paragraph; fields.tex Tag 0BU2 (lemma-infinite-galois-limit)

proof.text: Here the limit $C$ is the full prime-to-$p$ root limit $T=\varprojlim_{(m,p)=1}\mu_m(k)$. Explicitly, a compatible family $(z_m)_m$ in $T$ maps to $(z_{n_L})_L$ in $C$. Conversely, for $(c_L)_L\in C$ and an order $m$ choose any finite Galois $L$ with $m\mid n_L$ (Step 3 gives one with equality) and set $z_m=c_L^{n_L/m}$. Given two choices, a common finite Galois overfield and the transition formula of Step 2 show that these expressions agree. For $m\mid m'$, choose a common overfield for the two choices and compute $z_{m'}^{m'/m}=z_m$. Both constructions are homomorphisms, inverse to each other: recovering a coordinate $c_L$ permits choosing that very $L$ at order $n_L$. Each output coordinate depends on a single input coordinate through a power map between finite discrete groups; both maps are therefore continuous in the inverse-limit topologies.

source.place: Tag 0BUB (lemma-structure-decomposition-separable-closure), cofinality of the tame indices; explicit two-sided coordinate identification

proof.text: Use [lem-exc-tame-roots-product] to choose compatible primitive roots in $k$ and a topological-group isomorphism $T\cong\prod_{r\ne p}(\mathbf Z_r,+)$. Compose it with the continuous surjection of Step 4 and the coordinate isomorphism of Step 5. This gives $\theta$ with the same closed normal kernel $P$ and the required topological quotient. The finite-quotient assertion is already furnished by Step 4. The last identification uses the permitted choice of primitive roots, so it asserts no canonical trivialization of the Tate twist.
